name: Detect silence and speech segments in an audio file with FFmpeg

parameters.content:
## Detect silence and speech segments in an audio file with FFmpeg (free, no API)

Upload an audio file and get back a clean JSON report of every pause: exactly where each silence starts and ends, how long it is, and the derived speech segments in between (plus totals like percent silent). No API key, no account, no paid service - FFmpeg's `silencedetect` filter measures it for free on your own machine.

This is the same measurement technique behind the karaoke-caption templates in this pipeline (accurate word timing depends on knowing exactly where the speaker pauses), pulled out as a standalone analysis tool. Useful on its own for auto-chaptering long recordings, feeding real pause timestamps into any caption/subtitle workflow instead of guessing, or - with the optional output mode below - actually removing the dead air.

**Customization built in:** an Output dropdown lets you choose "Report only" (just the JSON), "Report + trimmed audio" (the detected speech segments stitched back-to-back with FFmpeg's concat filter into a silence-free file), or "Report + SRT markers" (the same segments written out as an SRT file so a video editor can jump straight to the non-silent parts).

### How it works

1. A form takes an audio file, a silence threshold in dB, a minimum silence duration in seconds, and an output mode: report only, a silence-trimmed audio file, or an SRT marker file.
2. The file is saved to a per-run temp folder and analyzed with FFmpeg's `silencedetect` filter - no output file is rendered at this stage, this only measures.
3. FFmpeg's own `Duration` line plus every `silence_start`/`silence_end` pair are parsed out of its stderr output.
4. Speech segments are derived as everything that is not silence, and a summary (silence count, total silent/speech time, percent silent) is added.
5. If "Report + trimmed audio" was chosen, every speech segment is cut and concatenated with FFmpeg's `concat` filter into one silence-free file. If "Report + SRT markers" was chosen, the same segments are written out as an SRT subtitle file instead. Either way the file is read back and returned alongside the report - otherwise the report alone is the output.

### Setup

Self-hosted n8n only - this uses Execute Command, which n8n Cloud disables. Install FFmpeg on the PATH of the process running n8n, and start n8n with `NODES_EXCLUDE="[]"` and `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO="/tmp"` - both are required or the file steps fail without a clear error.

## 1. Upload
Any format FFmpeg reads, plus a threshold, minimum pause length, and output mode (report only / report + trimmed file).

## 2. Analyze
FFmpeg's silencedetect filter measures every pause - no file is rendered.

## 3. Parse + derive + optional trim
Extracts real timestamps, derives speech segments, and - if requested - cuts+concatenates them into a silence-free file.

## Self-hosted only
Execute Command does not exist on n8n Cloud. See Setup in the overview.

nodes.name: Audio file and threshold form
nodes.notes: Entry point. Downstream nodes read the uploaded file's binary and the threshold/minimum-duration fields from here.

parameters.formTitle: Detect silence in an audio file

values.option: Report + SRT markers (speech segments as subtitle file)

parameters.formDescription: Upload an audio file, set a threshold, and choose the report only, a silence-trimmed audio file, or an SRT marker file for the speech segments.

nodes.name: Prepare Run
nodes.notes: Builds a per-run temp folder, detects the uploaded file's binary property name, and parses the numeric dB threshold and minimum silence duration.

nodes.name: Create the temp folder
nodes.notes: mkdir -p is safe to run again. This wipes json + binary, restored in the next node.

nodes.name: Restore the uploaded file
nodes.notes: Execute Command replaces the item with its own stdout/stderr/exitCode - re-attach the uploaded file's binary and the paths from Prepare Run.

nodes.name: Save the uploaded file to disk
nodes.notes: Writes the uploaded audio to the temp folder so FFmpeg (Execute Command) can read it by path.

nodes.name: Detect silence (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: Runs an analysis-only pass (no output file) - FFmpeg logs everything, including silencedetect's silence_start/silence_end lines, to stderr by default, which Execute Command captures separately in its own stderr field.

nodes.name: Parse the silence report
nodes.notes: Extracts the real Duration line and every silence_start/silence_end pair from FFmpeg's output, then derives the speech segments as everything that isn't silence.

nodes.name: Route by output mode
nodes.notes: Report only falls through with no output (the report itself already left the workflow via Parse the silence report). Trim and SRT each render their own file.

nodes.name: Build the trim filter (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: Turns the measured speechSegments into an FFmpeg atrim+concat filter_complex - reuses the real detected segments, doesn't re-guess anything.

nodes.name: Trim the silence (FFmpeg)
nodes.notes: Cuts every speech segment with atrim and stitches them back-to-back with concat - the output has zero of the detected silence in it.

nodes.name: Verify the trim succeeded
nodes.notes: Throws with the real FFmpeg error if the exit code was not 0, instead of silently returning a broken file path.

nodes.name: Read the trimmed audio back
nodes.notes: Reads the silence-free file off disk as binary output - the free-path deliverable, no external service involved.

nodes.name: Attach the report to the trimmed file
nodes.notes: Merges the full pause/speech report back onto the item so buyers get both the analysis and the trimmed file together.

nodes.name: Build SRT markers
nodes.notes: Turns the already-measured speech segments into an SRT file - a new code path, not another FFmpeg filter branch.

nodes.name: Save the SRT file to disk
nodes.notes: Writes the SRT marker file to the temp folder.

nodes.name: Read the SRT file back
nodes.notes: Reads the SRT file back off disk so it can be attached to the output.

nodes.name: Attach the report to the SRT file
nodes.notes: Same merge pattern as the trimmed-audio branch, applied to the SRT file.
